4. There is no dispute that Bank filed certificate case No. 15.B.S.B/87-88 against the petitioner for realizing of Tk. 38,28,963.97 and by letter dated 30.7.89 bank agreed to reduce the claim to Tk. 18,50,000/- provided petitioner paid the same by 25.8.89. There is also no dispute that petitioner failed to pay the said amount by that date and the petitioner Mills was sold in auction on 30.8.89 and thereafter petitioner sent on 11.9.89 the sum of Tk. 5 lac by a bank draft to the Bank. It appears from the aforesaid letter dated 30.7.89 that Senior Manager of the Bank informed the petitioner in response to its letter dated 29.6.89 that bank allowed it time upto 25.8.89 to pay the sum of Tk. 18,50,000/- as the last chance failing which bank's dues would be realized by selling the project of the petitioner on 30.8.89 through the certificate proceedings. It appears from copy of the Daily Ittefaq dated 6.8.89 that General Certificate Officer Moulvi Bazar fixed 30.8.89 for sale of the project of the petitioner. Admittedly auction sale took place on that date. Petitioner did not file any application either under section 22 or 23 of the P.D.R. Act 1913 before the certificate Officer for setting aside the sale. Instead thereof petitioner moved the vacation bench of this Court on 11.10.89 for stay and the vacation bench passed an order for maintaining status quo in respect of possession. Thereafter on 13.12.89 Rule was issued and operation of the auction held on 30.8.89 and handing over the mills and its property to the auction purchaser was stayed for a limited period and thereafter till disposal of the Rule. 

 5. Learned Advocate for the petitioner stated that after the Rule was discharged for default on 27.1.97 auction purchaser took delivery of possession and thereafter Rule was restored on 6.4.97. Again the Rule was discharged for default on 7.5.97 and again restored on 25.5.97. By a telex dated 20.8.89 Managing Director of the Bank asked the petitioner to pay Tk. 5 lac immediately out of the agreed sum of Tk. 18,50,000/- without prejudice to the claim of the certificate case and to pay the balance Tk. 13,50,000/- within December to avoid sale of its project through Court on 30th August. In pursuance of that telex message, petitioner did not pay the sum of Tk. 5 lac immediately and sent a bank draft for the said amount on 11.9.89 after the auction sale was held on 30.8.89. The said offer sent by the telex message was not accepted by the Board of Directors in its meeting held on 27.8.89. Thereafter pay order for Tk. 5 lac and cheque for Taka 13 lac and fifty thousand were returned to the petitioner. In view of the same we find no estoppel debarring the neither respondent No. 2 nor malafide on the part of the respondent bank. Rather we find that petitioner was never vigilant to pay the bank's dues in spite of the order passed in Misc. Case No. 9 of 1995 on 30.6.85 and filing of the Certificate Case in question on 15.10.87 and allowed the petitioner Mills to be sold in auction on 30.8.89.
